shortDescription: Brazil's industrial production undershot expectations in July, despite ending two consecutive months of contraction, government statistics agency IBGE said on Wednesday, suggesting the sector's recovery remains uneven.

children: Brazil's industrial production undershot expectations in July, despite ending two consecutive months of contraction, government statistics agency IBGE said on Wednesday, suggesting the sector's recovery remains uneven.
Output rose 0.2% in July from June, below the 0.6% increase expected by economists in a Reuters poll.
Production rose in three of the four main groups surveyed
Year-on-year, output was down 0.5%, while economists in a Reuters poll expected it to be flat.
The reading provides little evidence of a turnaround in the weakening industrial cycle, according to Pantheon Macroeconomics' chief Latin America economist Andres Abadia.
"Restrictive financial conditions increasingly are weighing on cyclical activity, and forward-looking indicators suggest that the slowdown has further to run," he said.
Brazil's benchmark Selic rate is currently at 14.00%, following four straight interest-rate cuts of 25 basis points each.
The central bank will hold its next monetary policy meeting on September 15 to 16.
